advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the per-proposal _write_link_event in backfill() so a CommandError logs and continues (or reports partial progress) instead of aborting the whole pass.
evidence: scripts/backfill_caused_by.py:68 `_links._write_link_event(bug_id, culprit_id, "caused_by", tracker_dir)` is not guarded
_seam.py:363 `Raises :class:`CommandError` carrying the exit code on failure (e.g. 75 = rebase/merge guard).`
transition_close.py:390 the close hook wraps the identical write in `except Exception: ... caused_by is best-effort; a failure must NEVER block the close`
advisory.finding: backfill()'s write loop does not wrap _write_link_event, which can raise CommandError (e.g. exit 75 rebase/merge guard); a failure mid-loop aborts the whole pass with a partial write and no report of which links were already drawn, unlike the 555e close hook which wraps the same call in try/except so it never fails hard.
scenarios: Rebase/merge in progress or a lock/commit failure while writing the Nth link

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether archived closed bugs are in scope; if so pass include_archived=True and add a test covering an archived closed bug.
evidence: scripts/backfill_caused_by.py:41 `for bug in rebar.list_tickets(status="closed", ticket_type="bug", repo_root=repo_root):`
No test in test_backfill_caused_by_heldout.py exercises an archived closed bug
advisory.finding: propose_caused_by iterates rebar.list_tickets(status="closed", ...) which defaults include_archived=False, so closed bugs that have been archived are silently excluded from the backfill — but archived legacy closed bugs are exactly the population this retroactive pass exists to cover.
scenarios: A legacy bug closed and later archived never receives its retroactive caused_by link

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that invokes main() (via monkeypatched sys.argv) asserting default runs write nothing and --write draws links, plus the printed output.
evidence: scripts/backfill_caused_by.py:73 `def main() -> None:` — argparse setup, `--write` branch, and the `[dry-run] ... would be written` / `wrote N caused_by link(s)` print output have no test

Neither tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py nor tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by_heldout.py references `main` (searches for `main` in these files return no calls; tests exercise `propose_caused_by`/`backfill` directly)
ABSENCE: a regression in main()'s branch selection (e.g. --write inverted, or dry-run accidentally calling backfill(write=True)) would not be caught by any current test
advisory.finding: The main() CLI entrypoint is untested: no test invokes main() or asserts its printed dry-run/write output or that the default (no --write) writes nothing. The script's user-facing safety contract ('--dry-run is the DEFAULT') is only verified at the backfill(write=False) library level, not through the argparse dispatch that actual invocation exercises.
